faq.title: Frequently asked questions

items.question: What account types exist?
items.answer: The platform manages several profiles (sole trader, SME, industrial SME, with more categories to be added later), each with a standard or premium access level.

items.question: What's the difference between a standard and a premium account?
items.answer: Your account's level determines which content and features you can access: some articles, courses or tools may be reserved for premium accounts.

items.question: Is the blog accessible without an account?
items.answer: Yes, the blog is publicly accessible. Courses and tools, on the other hand, require you to be logged in and depend on your access rights.

items.question: How does course certification work?
items.answer: A certificate is issued only once all of a course's completion conditions are met.

items.question: Are my content and media protected?
items.answer: Access to proprietary content (videos, images, documents) is checked every time it is opened. No web solution can fully prevent the copying of content that is displayed, but the platform strongly limits the possibilities for direct retrieval.

missions.howItWorks: A mission starts from a pretend amount. accueil.title: Start with “Today”
accueil.body: This page lists what is left to do. Each line leads to the exact place to settle it, and disappears once done.

accueil.title: Change the period in one click
accueil.body: Day, week, month, year: the figures follow the period you choose.

comptes.title: A transfer is not an expense
comptes.body: A transfer between your accounts changes neither your income nor your spending: it only moves money.

comptes.title: The starting balance matters
comptes.body: Give the balance the account had on a date: every calculation starts from there.

mouvements.title: Ticking is checking
mouvements.body: Compare each movement with your statement, then mark it “checked”: the home page stops reminding you.

mouvements.title: Search before filtering
mouvements.body: Search finds a label, a category or an amount; the filters then narrow it down.

budgets.title: A budget is a plan
budgets.body: Set what you plan to spend per category; the page then compares the plan with what you really spend.

budgets.title: The pace tells you where you stand
budgets.body: Read the cumulative spending against the even pace: above it, you spend faster than planned.

objectifs.title: Two different actions
objectifs.body: “Set aside” moves money to the goal; “Correct” only adjusts the figures.

objectifs.title: No date, no pressure
objectifs.body: The target date is optional: without it, the goal moves at your own pace.

dettes.title: Keep what you owe apart from what you are owed
dettes.body: Debts and receivables each have their section and their total.

dettes.title: Compare two ways to repay
dettes.body: The “Strategies” page shows how long and how much interest each order of repayment takes.

calendrier.title: Declare regular payments once
calendrier.body: Rent, subscriptions, salary: declare them and they come back by themselves at each due date.

calendrier.title: Confirm what happened
calendrier.body: When a due date arrives, say whether it took place: that is what adds it to your movements.

synthese.title: Read the sentence under the chart first
synthese.body: It says in words whether the curve rises or falls, before the detail of the figures.

synthese.title: Switch to day or week
synthese.body: The “By month / By week / By day” choice changes the step of every curve.

sante.title: An index is built up
sante.body: The more you fill in (income, debts, emergency fund), the more complete the index; a “not calculated” point says what is missing.

sante.title: One step at a time
sante.body: Pick the lowest dimension: it is the one that will raise the index most.

partage.title: Who paid, who owes what
partage.body: The expenses page works out the shares and proposes the fewest repayments.

partage.title: You keep control of your data
partage.body: You choose, kind of data by kind of data, what the other members see of you.

livret.name: Savings account (example)
livret.description: A savings account: the money stays available and does not fall, but earns little — often less than rising prices.

depot-terme.name: 12-month term deposit (example)
depot-terme.description: A sum locked for a set term, at a rate known in advance. Leaving before maturity costs part of the interest.

obligation-etat.name: 5-year government bond (example)
obligation-etat.description: A loan to the State, repaid at maturity with interest. Its price moves a little with rates meanwhile.

sukuk.name: Sukuk (example)
sukuk.description: A security compliant with Islamic finance, backed by a real asset: it pays a share of that asset’s income rather than interest.

fonds-diversifie.name: Diversified fund (example)
fonds-diversifie.description: A basket mixing bonds and shares: less variation than a single share, more expected return than a bond.

action-grande.name: Share of a large company (example)
action-grande.description: A part of an established company: more expected return over time, but years of decline are normal.

action-petite.name: Share of a small company (example)
action-petite.description: A part of a young or small company: can rise or fall a lot. Only for a small share, over a long time.

or.name: Gold (example)
or.description: A safe haven sought in times of crisis: pays nothing, its price varies strongly from one year to the next.
